sec-head.p: Standard AI models handle only one modality, but real-world data is inherently multimodal—text, images, and audio together. Multimodal AI fuses these inputs to deliver richer insights, higher accuracy, and more natural interactions without retraining for each data type.

ul: Image captioning and visual question answering
Video summarization with audio and text alignment
Multimodal search across images, documents, and speech
Healthcare diagnostics combining scans, reports, and patient notes
Ecommerce product understanding from images and descriptions
Voice assistants with visual context for smarter responses

step.body: Assess available data types (text, image, audio) and define the fusion strategy for your specific use case.
Design the pipeline for encoding, aligning, and fusing different modalities into a unified representation.
Develop and test each modality encoder and fusion layer independently before integration.
Test against cross-modal queries and measure accuracy, latency, and robustness across all inputs.
Deploy with monitoring for drift and ongoing support for model updates and scaling.

td: Baseline pipeline on sample data, evaluation report
Diagnose and improve an existing system

pricing.p: Multimodal systems delivered include the AI Video Summarizer and Image Captioning pipeline. Full case studies at shreyans.tech/ai-case-studies.

faq-item.faq-a: Multimodal AI is a system that processes and combines multiple data types—text, images, audio, and video—to produce richer outputs than single-modality models. It enables applications like image captioning, video understanding, and voice assistants with visual context.

It encodes each modality separately using specialized models, aligns them into a shared embedding space, and fuses the representations for joint reasoning. Common architectures include cross-attention transformers and early or late fusion strategies.
Common use cases include visual question answering, video summarization, multimodal search, healthcare diagnostics, ecommerce product understanding, and accessibility tools for the visually impaired.

faq-item.faq-q: How much does multimodal AI development cost?
faq-item.faq-a: A proof-of-concept starts at $2,000 to $5,000. A full production system ranges from $10,000 to $40,000 depending on modality complexity and data volume. Contact for a fixed-price estimate specific to your use case.

faq-item.faq-q: How long does it take to build a multimodal system?
faq-item.faq-a: A proof-of-concept typically takes 2 to 4 weeks. A full production system with evaluation and deployment typically takes 4 to 12 weeks depending on the number of modalities and integration requirements.
